report:
## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (no defect at or above the critical threshold; two doc Suggestions, one checklist Suggestion and three inconclusive checklist items)

This PR is ready to merge: the depth limit is iterative, runs in the place the criteria require, and its tests cover both sides of the limit, and nothing found reaches the critical threshold.
Rule applied: rule 6 — a finding or checklist FAIL below the threshold, or an INCONCLUSIVE item → APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

1. `docs/internal/agent/memory.md` line 183: the changed sentence says the "Three outer-shape caps … refuse such payloads", where "such payloads" means bundles with millions of cheap items. The new `MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH` limit is about nesting depth, not item count. The section heading still credits the caps to issue 186, but the depth limit comes from issue 309. The same issue-186 heading also covers the new depth-limit text in `docs/internal/mcp-server/tools.md` line 419. Behavior is unaffected. (raised by 1/5 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: no mechanism under discussion — the sentence describes what the caps protect against; git grep of view-head for agent/memory.md finds only doc links (architecture/overview.md, index.md, mcp-server/tools.md, mcp-server/transport.md, setup/config-loading.md, setup/preflight.md), no .sh/.py/.yml/workflow reader and no instruction file loading it; docs/internal is removed by .github/actions/vendor-plugin/vendor-slice.sh and published by no workflow -->
2. `docs/internal/agent/memory.md` line 183: the same sentence lists `MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH` among the caps that refuse "such payloads" (bundles with millions of cheap items). The depth limit does not address that threat; it addresses nesting that depends on the Python version. This is a clarity issue only. (raised by 1/5 agents) <!-- inertness: first-conjunct=held limb-one=held limb-two=held; evidence: no mechanism under discussion — the sentence describes what the caps protect against; git grep of view-head for agent/memory.md finds only doc links (architecture/overview.md, index.md, mcp-server/tools.md, mcp-server/transport.md, setup/config-loading.md, setup/preflight.md), no .sh/.py/.yml/workflow reader and no instruction file loading it; docs/internal is removed by .github/actions/vendor-plugin/vendor-slice.sh and published by no workflow -->
- VC-9: FAIL (suggestion) — The docstring asserts a deeply-nested JSON payload gets the "deeply nested" BundleFormatError on every Python version, whether json.loads raises RecursionError or parse_json's depth limit rejects it. [tests/unit/test_eval_golden.py:83]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Docstring (tests/unit/test_eval_golden.py:83-85) says 'A deeply-nested JSON payload' gets the 'deeply nested' error on every Python version. parse_json (src/sqllens/memory/io.py:134-148) maps RecursionError to _TOO_DEEP_MESSAGE and runs _enforce_depth_cap only after json.loads succeeds; json.JSONDecodeError (line 138-139) becomes 'invalid JSON: ...'. Counterexample: 10,000 '[' with no closing brackets (deep but malformed). On a Python where json.loads does not hit RecursionError at that depth (io.py:30-33 itself states only 3.11 raises under 1,000 levels, and the test/docstring contemplate versions where the depth limit does the rejecting), json.loads reaches end of input and raises JSONDecodeError, giving 'invalid JSON', not 'deeply nested'. The test's own payload is well-formed so the test passes, but the universal wording is unscoped; it holds only for well-formed deep payloads. I did not run it on multiple Python versions, so the counterexample is traced from the code, not executed.

  </details>

</details>

### ℹ️ Informational — Deferred (3)

<details><summary>3 items</summary>

- VC-10: INCONCLUSIVE (suggestion) — The comment asserts json.loads on Python 3.14 parses a 10,000-level nested-array payload without raising RecursionError, so only the explicit depth limit produces the "deeply nested" message there. [tests/unit/test_memory_schema_io.py:149]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  Repo side verified: src/sqllens/memory/io.py parse_json (134-148) calls json.loads, maps RecursionError to _TOO_DEEP_MESSAGE (140-145), then runs _enforce_depth_cap (98-113, iterative, MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH=64) which raises _TOO_DEEP_MESSAGE when loads succeeds; test at tests/unit/test_memory_schema_io.py:148-154 matches 'deeply nested'. So if loads succeeds on 3.14, only the depth cap yields that message. The factual claim that CPython 3.14's json.loads parses 10,000-level nested arrays without RecursionError depends on the CPython 3.14 _json.c / C-stack-limit behavior, which is not in the supplied views and I could not execute (no Python 3.14 run: `python3.14 -c 'import json; json.loads("["*10000+"1"+"]"*10000)'` not run). My recollection is that 3.14 uses a stack-pointer-based C recursion guard making this likely true, but it is unverified here.

  </details>

- VC-20: INCONCLUSIVE (important) — Per CLAUDE.md's Release notes rule, a change that is not developer-only (a new JSON bundle depth limit and newly supported Python 3.13/3.14 classifiers) ships a changelog.d/<PR>.<category>.md fragment and does not edit CHANGELOG.md or docs/external/release-notes.md. [pyproject.toml]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  FAIL stored INCONCLUSIVE (requirement quote names CLAUDE.md, a file it must stay out of): diff.patch touches only ci.yml, CLAUDE.md (Repo conventions hunk at ~line 154, not the Release notes paragraph), docs/internal/*, pyproject.toml, src/sqllens/eval/golden.py, src/sqllens/memory/io.py and two tests. No changelog.d/ file is added (grep for 'changelog.d' in the diff: no matches; head view changelog.d/ has no 309/321 fragment, newest is 315.changed.md from another PR). CHANGELOG.md and docs/external/release-notes.md are not edited (that half holds). But the PR adds a user-visible behavior (parse_json/import_memory now rejects bundles nested deeper than MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH=64 with 'bundle JSON is too deeply nested to parse safely') and newly declares Python 3.13/3.14 support in pyproject classifiers and CI; that is not developer-only, so CLAUDE.md line 130-134 requires a changelog.d/<PR>.<category>.md fragment, which is missing.

  </details>

- VC-26: INCONCLUSIVE (critical) — The `unit` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14, and passes on all four. [.github/workflows/ci.yml:38]

  <details><summary>Evidence</summary>

  criteria.json is a valid list of {criterion,text} objects and carries criterion 6, so it counts. The matrix half of the claim holds: .github/workflows/ci.yml:35-38 sets `python-version: ["3.11", "3.12", "3.13", "3.14"]` for jobs.unit, with fail-fast false, and setup-python uses that matrix value (line 46). The 'passes on all four' half cannot be settled by reading source. It needs actual CI run results for the py3.13 and py3.14 jobs, or a local pytest/pip install run on those interpreters (including dependency pins from requirements.txt and docker/requirements-drivers.txt resolving on 3.14). I did not run any of those and no CI results were supplied.

  </details>

</details>

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] On every Python version in CI's `unit` matrix, `parse_json` raises `BundleFormatError` whose message contains "deeply nested" for each of at minimum these well-formed payloads, at a total depth of 65 and of 10,000, where depth counts nested arrays and objects with the root container at depth 1: nested arrays with an array root; an object root whose single value is nested arrays; and nested objects, each object's single value being the next object.
- [ ] On every Python version in CI's `unit` matrix, `load_golden(payload, "json")` raises `BundleFormatError` whose message contains "deeply nested" for a 10,000-level nested-array payload.
- [ ] `parse_json` raises `BundleFormatError` whose message contains "deeply nested" when the parsed value's depth (nested arrays and objects, root container at depth 1) exceeds `MAX_BUNDLE_DEPTH = 64`, defined in `src/sqllens/memory/io.py`, checked by walking the parsed value iteratively, without recursion, after `json.loads` and before the "bundle root must be a JSON object" check; a well-formed payload of depth 64 is not rejected by this check.
- [ ] A valid JSON bundle carrying both a `sql_pairs` block with at least one pair and a `schema_docs` list still parses to the same `MemoryBundle` as before the change.
- [ ] `parse_json` still converts a `RecursionError` raised by `json.loads` into `BundleFormatError` whose message contains "deeply nested", shown by a test that makes `json.loads` raise `RecursionError`.
- [ ] The `unit` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14, and passes on all four.
- [ ] `pyproject.toml` lists the `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13` and `Programming Language :: Python :: 3.14` classifiers, and `requires-python` is still `>=3.11`.
- [ ] `CLAUDE.md`'s *Repo conventions* lists `Lint + unit + transport (py3.11)` and `Lint + unit + transport (py3.12)` as the required checks, and names the `py3.13` and `py3.14` unit jobs and `Connector tests (Postgres + MySQL)` as running on every PR without being required.
- [ ] The change leaves the Python matrix of `.github/workflows/dependency-audit.yml` unchanged (it keeps auditing 3.11 and 3.12 only); leaves `parse_json`'s `JSONDecodeError` handling unchanged (a deep payload that is also invalid JSON, and that 3.14's `json.loads` scans without `RecursionError`, keeps getting "invalid JSON" on Python 3.14); and leaves Python versions above 3.14 untested in CI and unlisted in the classifiers while `requires-python = ">=3.11"` still admits them.
